newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London quiet, Deng worries nag.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London quiet, Deng worries nag.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London were little changed on Wednesday as continuing worries about the health of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping kept investors at bay, dealers said.

The Hang Seng London Reference Index was 34.89 points higher at 13,141.21 by 1430 GMT but dealers said most of this rise was attributable to HSBC Holdings, up HK$2.00 from its Hong Kong close on the back of a firmer FTSE in London.

"We've had good days on Wall Street but Hong Kong can't take up the gauntlet. Deng Xiaoping's health is worrying the market and until we get that get that cleared up we will be restricted in how far we can go up," one dealer said.
Aside from HSBC, most stocks were unchanged, although Cheung Kong was reasonably well bid, dealers said.
In Hong Kong overnight, the Hang Seng closed 3.38 points higher at 13,106.32.
